definition-changed.answer: §2002:4 (entry 4.123) 'The request to execute a named method on a given object' and §2023:3.121 are the same words; 2002's 4.113 entry is only a cross-reference to it. The term names the same act in both editions, so the rule's scope is unchanged. SR3's 'invoke a method with the INVOKE statement or an inline invocation of a method' therefore names the same constructs.

definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 (entry 4.121) defines method as a procedural entity of a class definition; 2023 drops the entry and relies on 9.3.4, whose text is word for word §2002:9.3.4. The same source elements are methods in both editions, so the rule governs the same programs.

pending-clause.answer: §2002:9.3.5 differs from §2023:9.3.6 only in method RESOLUTION: 2023 adds signature matching and overload steps, 2002 binds by method-name alone. This rule restricts where a name may be written at compile time and does not rest on how an invocation is resolved; scope and evidence unchanged. §2002:9.3.5 itself sends SUPER's restricted search to 8.4.2.8, the clause this rule is in; the three permitted contexts are the ones 9.3.5 lists (INVOKE, inline invocation, object property).
